b: In the Croatian village of Čigoč, some of the most conspicuous residents live above the rooftops. White storks build bulky nests on traditional wooden houses, sharing the settlement with the people below.

Situated in Lonjsko Polje Nature Park beside the Tišina oxbow of the Sava River, the village is surrounded by wet meadows, pastures, and pools. These habitats provide feeding grounds close to the nests, allowing adult birds to gather frogs, insects, and other small animals for their young.

In 1994, the conservation foundation EuroNatur named Čigoč the first European Stork Village. The designation recognised the village’s importance for white storks and its long-standing relationship between people, traditional farming, and wildlife. It also launched an initiative that would connect stork villages across Europe.

The wooden houses are part of this story. Their rooftops provide nesting places, while the surrounding agricultural landscape helps sustain the birds. During the breeding season, a walk through the village offers a chance to watch adults tending their nests and travelling between the rooftops and nearby feeding grounds.
